gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a single instrument-measured figure for any triple laptop screen extender. The nearest named lab test of a FOPO triple, Notebookcheck's of the 12-inch 1080p model (2022-07-23), measured 177.4 cd/m² average brightness and 247:1 contrast. That is well below the 250–300 nit and 800–1000:1 figures makers quote across this category.
standout_why: I compared the uperfect.com '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders' page (cited, opened 2026-11-21) and the ChatGPT answers that cite Newegg (Hyangin Z3) and fopomonitor.com (S788). The uperfect page gives only maker figures: 300 nits for the FOPO S9G and '100% sRGB' for others, with no named tester. ChatGPT's answers already warn that the specs are 'manufacturer-advertised… not hands-on test rankings' and 'not independently verified measurements'. So the rivals already say nothing has been measured, and they add no numbers. What I add is real measurements of related models: a FOPO triple, a KYY triple weighed on a scale, and a 16-inch triple. None of them is an exact 15–16-inch 1920×1200 candidate, so they give context but don't decide the pick.
decides: This doesn't change the pick, because no named reviewer or lab has measured any candidate: FOPO S788, S980, S11 or S9G, Hyangin Z3, INVZI MagHub Trio Go, APILDELLA, NGTeco or Aura Triple Go 16 Plus. Brightness, contrast and weight in the table can only be maker figures. The page should say so and use the named tests of related models only as a caution. Notebookcheck measured FOPO's 12-inch triple at about 60–70% of the brightness this class usually claims. PCWorld weighed KYY's triple at about 6.5 lb against a 1.6 kg claim. So shoppers shouldn't choose between near-identical 300-nit spec sheets on brightness or weight. The deciding factors stay as the page rules set them: the video path (native Alt Mode vs driver) and screen count.

findings.product: FOPO Triple Monitor Extender 12-inch (1920×1080), the older FOPO triple and not a candidate
findings.label: Measured brightness (average / centre)
findings.value: 177.4 cd/m² average; 185 cd/m² centre (max point 193.1 cd/m²)
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review: Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Measured by Allen Ngo, Notebookcheck, in a review published 2022-07-23, using Notebookcheck's colorimeter and Calman method. Brightness distribution was 85%. This is a 12-inch 1080p unit, not a 15–16-inch 1920×1200 model.

findings.label: Measured contrast and black level
findings.note: Allen Ngo, Notebookcheck, 2022-07-23. For comparison, FOPO rates the S11 at 800:1 and the S1, S7 and S10 at 1000:1 (our records, read 2026-11-17/18). The 12-inch unit measured roughly a quarter to a third of those ratings.

findings.label: Measured colour gamut and accuracy
findings.value: 79% sRGB, 79% AdobeRGB, 77.1% Display P3; ΔE2000 ColorChecker 4.59 average (10.04 max), greyscale 6.8
findings.note: Allen Ngo, Notebookcheck, 2022-07-23, measured with Calman. Calibration brought ColorChecker ΔE down to 0.84. CCT 7468 K, gamma 2.09.

findings.label: Measured response time and PWM
findings.value: 29.2 ms black-white; 31.6 ms 50–80% grey; no PWM at any brightness
findings.note: Allen Ngo, Notebookcheck, 2022-07-23. On their test laptop, an HP Pavilion Plus 14 with two USB-C DP ports, Windows saw each screen as an ordinary external monitor.

findings.label: Brightness Notebookcheck says it typically sees on add-on laptop extenders
findings.source_title: Monduo 16 Pro Duo in review: A built-in triple-monitor setup for laptops (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Christian Hintze, Notebookcheck, 2023-05-14: 'we saw examples with about 250 nits of brightness, a maximum of 1080p and 60 Hz.' This describes similar products in general; it is not a measurement of any candidate.

findings.product: Monduo 16 Pro Duo (2× 16-inch 2560×1600), a reference for the size class and not a 1920×1200 candidate
findings.label: Measured brightness, contrast and power per panel
findings.value: 389 / 422 cd/m² average (left / right); 1058:1 / 1229:1 contrast; about 15 W per display (about 30 W for both)
findings.note: Christian Hintze, Notebookcheck, 2023-05-14. Also measured: 99.9% / 100% sRGB, 97% DCI-P3, 1.9 kg weight, no PWM. The BOE NE160QDM-NY3 panels are 2560×1600, outside the 1920×1200 question. This is the only lab-measured 16-inch two-added-screen unit I found. Monduo specifies at least 15 W of USB power per display.

findings.product: KYY Laptop Triple Screen Extender (three 1080p screens; URL suggests X90G, not confirmed in text)
findings.label: Weight on the reviewer's scale vs maker claim
findings.value: about 6.5 lb measured vs 1.6 kg (about 3.5 lb) claimed by KYY
findings.source_title: KYY Triple Laptop Screen Extender review: The new king of the coffeehouse (PCWorld)
findings.note: Weighed by Mark Hachman, PCWorld, 2026-04-28. Extender alone about 6.5 lb; with the laptop about 10 lb. Measured dimensions were 15.2 × 9 × 1.5 in, which the article says differ from KYY's. This is a 1080p unit and not a candidate. It shows that maker weight claims in this category can be badly off.

findings.label: Whole-system battery drain at idle with screens lit
findings.value: 15% of a 99 Wh battery in 33 minutes (≈27 W whole system)
findings.source_title: KYY Triple Laptop Screen Extender review (PCWorld)
findings.note: Mark Hachman, PCWorld, 2026-04-28. My arithmetic: 0.15 × 99 Wh = 14.85 Wh over 0.55 h ≈ 27 W. This includes the laptop itself, so it is not the extender's own draw. KYY states the extender consumes 28 W. The reviewer judged the screens 'a bit faint' by eye; no meter was used.
